FR-001.title: Every packaged production launch MUST initiate exactly one update check after the application can present Overseer-facing status.

FR-002.title: The startup update check MUST run without blocking normal application readiness or local operation.

FR-003.title: The application MUST compare the installed application version with published release versions using semantic-version precedence.

FR-004.title: The application MUST offer only a strictly newer release that is eligible for the installed release channel, running platform, and running architecture.

FR-005.title: When an eligible update exists, the application MUST present the Overseer with the installed version, available version, release notes when supplied, and a choice to update now or continue without updating.

FR-006.title: The application MUST NOT download, stage, replace, or restart for an update until the Overseer explicitly accepts the offered update.

FR-007.title: Deferring or dismissing an update MUST leave the current application fully usable and MUST suppress another prompt for the same release during that application run.

FR-008.title: The update flow MUST select exactly one artifact that matches the running platform and architecture and MUST reject missing or ambiguous matches.

FR-009.title: The application MUST verify every downloaded update against publisher-provided integrity or authenticity evidence before staging it.

FR-010.title: Missing, malformed, or mismatched verification evidence MUST prevent the update from being staged or applied.

FR-011.title: The update flow MUST accept only a replacement unit compatible with the installed application's platform-specific package layout.

FR-012.title: The application MUST report checking, downloading, verifying, staging, ready-to-restart, and failed states to the Overseer without exposing sensitive values.

FR-013.title: A prepared update MUST require a separate Overseer decision before the application restarts to apply it.

FR-014.title: Applying an update MUST use the application's normal ordered shutdown so owned resources are released before replacement begins.

FR-015.title: A successfully applied update MUST relaunch the application at the accepted newer version.

FR-016.title: If replacement or relaunch fails, the update process MUST retain or restore the last working installation and MUST NOT report success.

FR-017.title: Update discovery, download, verification, staging, replacement, and relaunch failures MUST NOT corrupt or modify sessions, player configurations, credentials, preferences, or other user-owned data.

FR-018.title: Failure to check for or prepare an update MUST NOT cause application startup to fail or disable local operation.

FR-019.title: The application MUST prevent concurrent update checks or installations from creating competing state or replacement attempts.

FR-020.title: Unversioned development builds MUST NOT perform a production update check or present a production update prompt.

FR-021.title: Every governed release for a supported target MUST embed its exact release version in the packaged application.

FR-022.title: Every governed release MUST publish the compatible target artifacts and their verification evidence as one complete release before any installed application can discover it.

FR-023.title: Release publication MUST withhold an update from discovery when any required supported-target artifact or verification record is absent or invalid.

FR-024.title: The update feature MUST support the existing governed targets: Windows amd64, Windows arm64, Linux amd64, Linux arm64, and macOS arm64.

FR-025.title: Update diagnostics MUST identify the failed stage and provide an actionable next step while excluding credentials, authorization values, and user document contents.

context: reference: official Wails v3 self-update tutorial and updater guide
area: application startup and Overseer host lifecycle
area: five-target portable packaging and tagged release publication
constraint: test-owned Go resources use immediate t.Cleanup registration with uncancelled bounded cleanup contexts when needed
intent: Let the Overseer discover and safely apply a trusted newer Fallout Terminal release during application startup without making updates an availability dependency.
expectations: No new update account, license service, or private update backend.
No background update service while the application is closed.
approach: Use the pinned Wails updater headlessly for discovery, transfer, extraction, and GitHub asset-digest verification behind a launch-scoped application manager and private revisioned bridge. After verification, validate manifest v2 and use a temporary helper to atomically replace and recover the complete portable application unit through normal ordered shutdown.

decisions.decision: Use pinned Wails updater headlessly behind an application-owned manager
decisions.why: It supplies proven discovery, transfer, extraction, progress, and verification while preserving separate offer and restart consent
decisions.rejected: CheckAndInstall with the built-in updater window

decisions.decision: Use GitHub release asset SHA-256 metadata as verification evidence
decisions.why: It fails closed through Wails verification while preserving the constitutionally required exact five-archive inventory
decisions.rejected: Publish checksum sidecars or a signed aggregate manifest

decisions.decision: Replace complete portable units with an application-owned temporary helper
decisions.why: Current archives contain resource trees that the Wails executable-only restart target cannot replace safely
decisions.rejected: Bare executable updater assets or a private Wails fork

decisions.decision: Advance artifact manifest to schema v2 with canonical version
decisions.why: The staged tree must prove target, structure, and equality with the accepted release without executing downloaded code
decisions.rejected: Trust only the tag or run the staged executable before restart approval

decisions.decision: Start one check from an event-first update-status handshake
decisions.why: The frontend can present status before discovery emits and snapshot revisions close startup races
decisions.rejected: Emit the first update event at the end of App.Start

decisions.decision: Expose three private desktop methods and one named update event
decisions.why: Explicit protobuf-governed decisions preserve the narrow privileged boundary and make stale attempts rejectable
decisions.rejected: Direct framework events, a generic dispatcher, or a public RPC

decisions.decision: Keep deferment and prepared state launch-scoped with only a recovery journal persisted
decisions.why: This matches one-run suppression and preserves actionable post-shutdown recovery without a permanent skip policy
decisions.rejected: Persist skipped versions or abandoned stages indefinitely

plan.key_finding: The governed archives are complete portable trees, so Wails can verify and extract them but an application-owned helper must replace the whole unit while GitHub asset digests preserve the exact five-asset release contract
